01: Over Jefferson Barracks near St. Louis, Albert Berry jumps from a Benoist biplane at 1,500 feet: the first documented parachute jump from a powered airplane.
02: The B-50 bomber Lucky Lady II lands at Fort Worth, Texas, after 94 hours and four refuelings in the air: the first airplane to circle the world nonstop.
03: Alexander Graham Bell is born in Edinburgh, Scotland.
04: Nine motor clubs with 1,500 members meet in Chicago and form the American Automobile Association, to press for roads fit for cars.
05: At Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, with President Truman in the audience, Winston Churchill says 'an Iron Curtain has descended across the Continent.'
The Homebrew Computer Club meets for the first time, in Gordon French's garage in Menlo Park, California. Steve Wozniak said it inspired him to design the Apple I.
06: The Supreme Court rules 7 to 2 against Dred Scott, who had first sued for his freedom at the Old Courthouse in St. Louis in 1846, holding that he could not be a citizen.
07: Soldiers of the U.S. 9th Armored Division capture the Ludendorff Bridge at Remagen intact and cross the Rhine. The bridge collapsed ten days later.
08: Daytona Beach holds its first stock car race, on a 3.2-mile course of beach and road. The sandy turns become nearly impassable and the race is stopped three laps early.
09: At Hampton Roads, Virginia, USS Monitor and CSS Virginia fight for hours at close range to a draw: the first battle between ironclad warships.
10: Three Flags Day: in St. Louis the Spanish flag came down on March 9, the French flag flew for a day, and now the American flag goes up. Upper Louisiana joins the United States.
In Boston, Alexander Graham Bell speaks the first words heard clearly over a telephone: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'
11: The Great Blizzard of 1888 begins. Over four days it buries the Northeast under as much as 58 inches of snow and kills about 400. New York later moved its wires underground.
12: Eight days after taking office, President Roosevelt explains the banking crisis to the nation by radio: the first 'fireside chat'.
At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee hands in 'Information Management: A Proposal', the plan that became the World Wide Web.
13: From his back garden in Bath, England, William Herschel spots Uranus with a telescope he built himself. He first took it for a comet.
14: Eli Whitney is granted his patent for the cotton gin.
Casey Jones is born in southeastern Missouri (his family Bible says 1863). The Illinois Central engineer died at the throttle of No. 382 in 1900, the only person killed in the wreck.
15: Symbolics.com is registered: the first .com domain name on the internet.
16: At Auburn, Massachusetts, Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fueled rocket. It rises 41 feet, flies for 2.5 seconds and lands in a cabbage field.
17: The nuclear submarine USS Skate becomes the first submarine to surface at the North Pole. Her crew scatters the ashes of polar explorer Sir Hubert Wilkins there.
18: The Tri-State Tornado touches down in Shannon County, Missouri, and runs 219 miles across Missouri, Illinois and Indiana. It kills at least 695, the deadliest tornado in U.S. history.
19: The Standard Time Act puts the railroads' time zones into federal law, with the Interstate Commerce Commission to draw the lines, and adds daylight saving time.
20: At the railway station in Terowie, South Australia, Gen. Douglas MacArthur, just out of the Philippines, tells reporters: 'I came through and I shall return.'
21: St. Louis native Jack Dorsey sends the first tweet: 'just setting up my twttr'.
22: Intel introduces the Pentium processor: 3.1 million transistors, running at 60 MHz.
23: Lewis and Clark leave Fort Clatsop on the Pacific coast and start for home. They reached St. Louis six months later, on September 23.
Gus Grissom and John Young fly Gemini 3, the first crewed Gemini, in a spacecraft built by McDonnell in St. Louis. Young smuggles a corned beef sandwich aboard.
24: The Great Escape: 76 Allied airmen crawl out of Stalag Luft III through the tunnel 'Harry'. Three reached home; 50 of those recaptured were shot on Hitler's order.
Just after midnight the tanker Exxon Valdez strikes Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound, Alaska, and spills more than 10 million gallons of crude oil.
25: In Wales, the Swansea and Mumbles Railway begins carrying fare-paying passengers in horse-drawn carriages: the world's first passenger railway service.
Norman Borlaug is born on a farm in Saude, Iowa. His high-yield, disease-resistant wheat led the Green Revolution and won him the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize.
26: The spinach growers of Crystal City, Texas, have a statue of Popeye standing in town, in thanks for what the sailor did for sales of their crop.
27: Marconi sends a wireless message across the English Channel, from Wimereux, France, to the South Foreland Lighthouse in England.
28: On the Etang de Berre in France, Henri Fabre takes off from the water in his Hydravion: the first seaplane flight. The longest of four hops that day is about 600 meters.
29: An ice jam upstream stops Niagara Falls. For about 40 hours almost no water goes over; waterwheels stop and the mills shut down.
30: Jethro Tull is baptised at Basildon, England. His horse-drawn seed drill of 1701 sowed seed in neat rows at an even depth, in place of scattering it by hand.
31: At the Harland and Wolff yard in Belfast, the keel of the Titanic is laid. She was launched on May 31, 1911, and sank on April 15, 1912.
